cells.tense: Right now the pick is being made, and the pen is still in your hand.
cells.act: share your strength where it is needed
cells.ask: Someone near you is in fog too. Hand them one clear thing you can see. Say it plain and then stop — no steering, no checking whether they used it. That's all.
cells.core:
When the road isn't visible yet, you don't wait for it. Enough light for the next step is what you've got, and you move on it — that's the navigating, and it's working. What you know doesn't come from argument; it arrives as a direction, and you follow it because you recognize it.

What this balance is free to feed next is somewhere else. Someone near you is in fog too. Hand them one clear thing you can see — offered plain, no push behind it — and the next step is theirs to take. You don't have to know where it leads or what it fixes. Say it, and be done.
cells.sheetLine: You move on enough light, and can hand some over.

cells.tense: You are scanning the whole road ahead, and it is arriving without you.
cells.act: distinguish what is yours from what you borrowed
cells.ask: Write the pulls on you down in one column and note where each came from. Name the two that are yours, then pick one and move before the week ends. The rest can wait where they are.
cells.core:
You can follow one direction at a time. Under pressure you try to follow five — all urgent, none actually picked — and the decision gets pushed forward, handled by a plan that hasn't happened yet. Everything looks like it needs answering now, so nothing gets chosen. The road ahead is doing the driving.

The way back goes through sorting, not deciding. Some of those pulls aren't yours. Set them side by side on paper, mark where each one came from, and say which are yours. Two at most. Then move on one of those, and leave the others outside for now — they'll still be there.

cells.tense: A direction was picked once, and you have not left the doorway since.
cells.act: rest in the result of the tending
cells.ask: Something you grew is finished enough. Put your hands on it — walk around it, use it, read it — and let yourself take pleasure in it, with no next step attached. That's the whole act.
cells.core:
There is a doorway behind you that used to be a direction. You wait at it and say you're about to go through. The year and the moving are in the past tense now, and so is the light you were following — still there, unattended, while the present goes on without any steering at all.

Pushing harder won't do it: no amount of thought puts a direction back. So turn toward the thing you already grew — the work, the place, the person, whatever your care made — and take pleasure in it. Feel the weight of the finished thing, and don't draft the next one. The pick revives from there, not from here.

cells.tense: The direction gets set, and by your own telling you had nothing to do with it.
cells.act: let resources flow to the person who needs them
cells.ask: When a stuck decision is brought to you, say the direction you can see for them, once, plainly. Stay beside them while they try it on. Let it be refused. Then notice, out loud to yourself, that you did that.
cells.core:
The direction gets set in the rooms near you. People come to a decision clearer, or pointed somewhere they weren't before, because you held the question open and they didn't have to do it alone. Ask you, and none of it happened. The hand that steered says it stayed outside.

One thing to do, and not a large one: let what you know reach the person who needs it. Say the direction you can see for them, once, and stay beside them while they try it on. Let them refuse it. The weight you've been carrying will show itself then — which doesn't undo the modesty. It only puts the steering where it truly was.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person once had a calling they are still standing behind — the record says too little of this capacity is present in this seat, not what closed it. A reader could reasonably say no door was ever theirs to walk through, or that the pull they feel now is the first one. The asks survive being wrong: each is one small act in the present, false only in its framing, and useful even if the read of history is off. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is 'Radiance flows from genuine development' — it flatters the map, not the life, so it stays out of the glass. All four asks are Support's own acts, copied word for word from the plan, done small in the seat of Imagination.
